## The R runs here, in this page {#s00-webr}

::: {.slide-kicker}
No install · no account · nothing to download
:::

::: {.lede-min}
The grey boxes below are real R. Press **Run** and the code executes inside your browser — there is no server, and nothing you type is sent anywhere.
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-text}
```{webr-r}
# Edit anything here, then press Run.
x <- rnorm(10, mean = 100, sd = 15)

round(mean(x), 2)
```
:::

::: {.try-this}
Press **Run** a few times without changing anything. The mean comes out different every time.
:::

```{webr-r}
#| context: setup
# Hidden: enlarges text and tightens margins on every plot in the deck (spec §6.2).
# If this cell errors, the extension never re-enables the Run buttons, so keep it trivial.
setHook("before.plot.new", function() par(cex = 1.6, mar = c(3.6, 3.8, 1.6, 0.8), mgp = c(2.3, 0.8, 0)))
```

```{=html}
<div class="deck-facts">
  <div>
    <span>Nine seminars</span>
    One idea each, in the order we meet them. Nothing here needs the seminar
    before it to make sense.
  </div>
  <div>
    <span>Moving around</span>
    Arrows or space step through. <kbd>Esc</kbd> shows every slide at once,
    <kbd>M</kbd> opens the contents.
  </div>
  <div>
    <span>Writing on it</span>
    <kbd>B</kbd> opens a blackboard and <kbd>C</kbd> draws straight over a
    slide, so worked examples happen in front of you.
  </div>
</div>
```

::: {.slide-footer}
First run takes a few seconds while R loads. After that it is instant.
:::
